verdict.rationale: Make ships its own MCP server that lets AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT run scenarios and view or modify account contents. It also provides Make Skills so those assistants can build scenarios. That gives users natural-language operation, but only through an external AI client; no native in-product natural-language command interface is evidenced. missing for 10: native in-product natural-language command interface, hands-on or independent corroboration of natural-language operation quality, documented scope limits of what natural-language commands can manage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Make MCP server allows AI systems, such as large language models (LLMs), to run scenarios and manage the contents of your Make account.
View and modify scenarios and their related entities (e.g., connections, webhooks, and data stores)

Make Skills are Markdown files that help your assistant reliably perform Make-specific tasks, including building scenarios, configuring modules, and connecting to Make MCP server or third-party services.
